chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Aban ibn Uthman from Bakr ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"For the young boy (who has not reached puberty), it is not permissible to trim (shorten the hair), but he must shave (the head)."

As for that which indicates that for whoever performs the Hajj of Islam, trimming (shortening the hair) is sufficient, the first report is the evidence, and to add clarification to that is what has been narrated:

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Trimming (shortening the hair, as opposed to complete shaving)
key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: A young boy who has not yet reached puberty
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَام: The first obligatory pilgrimage performed by a Muslim
key_terms.يُقَصِّر: To trim or shorten the hair (leaving some length)

ai.seo_question: What is the required method of hair cutting for a young boy performing his first obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific ritual requirement for a young boy performing his first Hajj, mandating complete shaving (halq) rather than mere trimming (taqsir) to ensure the validity of his Hajj al-Islam. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the obligations of minors and adults, noting that while trimming may suffice for others, the full removal of hair is essential for the boy's initial pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the precision required in Hajj rituals to fulfill the religious duty completely.
